name: Amoeba Device Patterns — Reusable Templates for Network Devices
description: Patterns for injecting amoeba (RustDesk + monitoring + mesh) into network devices. Each pattern defines how to discover, monitor, and manage a class of device.

ssh_install: 2. Install monitoring script: scp amoeba-heartbeat.sh root@{ip}:/tmp/
amoeba_injection.heartbeat_script:
#!/bin/sh
# amoeba-heartbeat.sh — GL.iNet router heartbeat
DATA=$(cat <<EOF
{"type":"router","ip":"$(ip -4 addr show br-lan|grep inet|awk '{print $2}')",
"uptime":"$(cat /proc/uptime|awk '{print $1}')",
"load":"$(cat /proc/loadavg|awk '{print $1,$2,$3}')",
"mem_free":$(free|grep Mem|awk '{print $4}'),
"clients":$(ip neigh|grep -c REACHABLE),
"wifi_clients":$(for i in ra0 ra1 rax0 rax1;do iwinfo $i assoclist 2>/dev/null;done|grep -c dBm),
"timestamp":"$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"}
EOF
)
curl -s -X POST http://192.168.4.244:8080/api/heartbeat -d "$DATA" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 2>/dev/null || true

rustdesk.reason: RustDesk requires X11/Wayland display — routers are headless. Use SSH + heartbeat instead.
rustdesk.alternative: SSH tunnel + web admin relay via amoeba proxy

gl_mt6000_router.role: Main router — ONE router for both houses

amoeba_injection.method: HTTP monitoring — no SSH available on managed switches
amoeba_injection.monitoring_script:
#!/bin/bash
# amoeba-switch-monitor.sh — monitor TP-Link switch via HTTP
SWITCH_IP=$1
HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --connect-timeout 3 http://$SWITCH_IP/)
if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ]; then
  echo '{"type":"switch","ip":"'$SWITCH_IP'","http_status":'$HTTP_CODE',"alive":true,"timestamp":"'$(date -u +%FT%TZ)'"}'
else
  echo '{"type":"switch","ip":"'$SWITCH_IP'","http_status":'$HTTP_CODE',"alive":false,"timestamp":"'$(date -u +%FT%TZ)'"}'
fi
